svg.title: From Dials to a Recurring Account
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-cold-call-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: From Dials to a Recurring Account; subtitle: Touch volume and the test-load conversion, per Dennis Brown and Matt Krause; chart type: funnel; caption: Phone-built brokers win on volume and follow-up. One 'we don't use brokers' prospect became a $150 test load and roughly $20,000 a year in profit.; assumptions note: Stages mix units (monthly touches, daily calls, touches per close, loads), so stage values show order of magnitude, not a single cohort conversion rate.; note: Sources - Matt Krause (NF0itNMuQvY, r0gf3CDabxw) and FreightBrokers with Dennis Brown (BCLv7SfCxIo, kc6-g1EZ0Fk, knW5LzcUJIw).; stages: label: Monthly touches per yes; value: 300; display: ~300 touches/month; conversion: About one shipper yes per ~300 monthly touches (Krause); detail: Krause runs 10-20 nightly touches after burning out at 100 a day.; label: Daily dial floor; value: 50; display: 50 calls/day; conversion: Brown's minimum; brokers who stop prospecting stop growing; detail: Retire 'did I catch you at a bad time' - Gong figures put it under 1%, about 40% worse than average.; label: Touches to close; value: 12; display: 8-12 touches; conversion: 6-8 is reasonable; it never closes on the first call; detail: Follow-up across phone, email, LinkedIn and face-to-face carries the deal.; label: Test load booked; value: 1; display: $150 gross profit; conversion: A 'we don't use brokers' prospect won with one test load; detail: Take three of five loads you can cover rather than committing to five and covering three.; label: Recurring account; value: 1; display: ~$20,000/year; conversion: Over $100,000 across 5+ years from that single pet food shipper; detail: Send the handover email the moment the carrier is confirmed, with carrier, pickup time, driver and the driver's direct number.

text.title: From Dials to a Recurring Account
text.tspan: From Dials to a Recurring Account

circle.title: label: Monthly touches per yes; value: 300; display: ~300 touches/month; conversion: About one shipper yes per ~300 monthly touches (Krause); detail: Krause runs 10-20 nightly touches after burning out at 100 a day.

label: Daily dial floor; value: 50; display: 50 calls/day; conversion: Brown's minimum; brokers who stop prospecting stop growing; detail: Retire 'did I catch you at a bad time' - Gong figures put it under 1%, about 40% worse than average.

label: Touches to close; value: 12; display: 8-12 touches; conversion: 6-8 is reasonable; it never closes on the first call; detail: Follow-up across phone, email, LinkedIn and face-to-face carries the deal.

label: Test load booked; value: 1; display: $150 gross profit; conversion: A 'we don't use brokers' prospect won with one test load; detail: Take three of five loads you can cover rather than committing to five and covering three.

label: Recurring account; value: 1; display: ~$20,000/year; conversion: Over $100,000 across 5+ years from that single pet food shipper; detail: Send the handover email the moment the carrier is confirmed, with carrier, pickup time, driver and the driver's direct number.

text.title: Assumptions: Stages mix units (monthly touches, daily calls, touches per close, loads), so stage values show order of magnitude, not a single cohort conversion rate.
